newsitem.title: MEXICO: Penoles seen bidding strong for Mahr Tunel.
newsitem.headline: Penoles seen bidding strong for Mahr Tunel.

text.p: Mexico's Industrias Penoles, the world's largest refined silver producer, is seen bidding strongly in the auction for Peru's Mahr Tunel lead-zinc-silver mines, analysts said on Friday.

All expectations are for Penoles to put forward a good offer for Mahr Tunel because last month the Mexican giant won the privatization auction for Peru's Oroya refinery complex -- only around 30 miles (50 km) from the mines in the central Peruvian highlands.
"Now that Penoles has Oroya, it is favoured as well in the Mahr Tunel auction," Valores Finamex mining analyst Christoper Albi said in a report.

"I reckon Penoles will want that mine more than the others bidding (in the auction). It will reduce third party costs for the refinery and makes sense," said Sebastian Barry-Taylor, mining analyst with Ing Barings in Mexico City. "They will bid strongly but within logical limits," he added.
Mahr Tunel is a segment of the huge state miner Centromin on the block from the Peruvian government. Mahr Tunel controls the San Cristobal and Andaychagua mines in the Andes.
Last year, San Cristobal produced 680,000 dry tonnes of ore containing zinc, lead, copper and silver, amd Andaychagua produced about 395,000 dry tonnes of ore containing silver, lead and zinc.

Centromin spokesman Enrique Olivares said Thursday that the government had fixed a $50 million minimum bid price for Mahr Tunel. The successful bidder would also have to promise to invest a minimum of $60 million over the next five years.

But Centromin has put back the privatisation date a little over a month as three interested companies requested more time to prepare offers. Proposals should now be presented July 14 and the opening of envelopes is scheduled for July 18.

Penoles confirmed on Friday its interest in the auction and stressed that parent company Industrias Penoles would make any offer and it would be without any partner. "Any bid will come from the parent company," a spokesman told Reuters.
Centromin on Thursday listed seven foreign companies and four local ones interested in Mahr Tunel.
Two of those foreign companies listed were Industrias Penoles and Minera Penoles del Peru, a subsidiary of the Mexican mining giant established several years ago as an exploratory miner in Peru.
